new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The quotation was checked again. The reported passage is a composite of Google Books volume-feed snippets, all present in the named files under gbooks_feeds/ and carry "17.5 Phonology Nalu has a seven - vowel system ( Table 17.1) with contrastive length. Table 17.1 Nalu vowel system..";, and carry ".. Nalu. There is evidence for tone in Nalu ( see Section 17.10), but this must remain the object of future studies. 17.5.1 A note on consonant clusters and phonotactics NC clusters are frequent in my data.."; shows the running head "390 SEIDEL 17.4 Typological features of Nalu 17.5 Phonology", confirming p. 390 (the held OUP detailed contents at give 17.5/17.5.1/17.5.2 = p. 390, 17.6 = p. 391).…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for word stress is given. The only modern primary description (Seidel 2024, 29-pp grammar sketch) treats Nalu prosody under tone: there is evidence for tone (grammatical tone, cf. sec. 17.10), left for future study. Seidel 2015 adds that only grammatical tone is unequivocally attested and lexical tone, if present, does not surface on words in isolation. Neither source (as far as visible) mentions stress or accent, so Nalu is a (probable) tone language with no word-stress statement.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author explicitly defers tonal analysis ('must remain the object of future studies'). Seidel 2015 notes lexical tone is unconfirmed and would not appear on isolated words.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology section of a grammar sketch based on documentary fieldwork (2011-2012) in Koukouba and Katoufoura, Guinea; pitch-contour figures (17.1-17.4) in the chapter concern phrase-level grammatical tone on verb forms, not word stress. CAVEAT: both quotations were recovered only as Google Books snippets (saved as feed XML); the full page was not opened, so a stress remark elsewhere in sec. 17.5 cannot be fully excluded, although in-volume searches pairing Nalu with stress/stressed/accent return zero hits.
new_statements.identity_note: Seidel 2024 (and the ELAR deposit) describe the Nalu of Koukouba and Katoufoura, northern Guinean coast (Kanfarandé, Boké); Glottolog tags the reference 'Nalu of Koukouba in Guinea = Nalu [naj]'. No separate glottocode; nalu1240 has no dialect children. Wilson 2007 is expected to reflect the Guinea-Bissau (Cacine/Tombali) variety; Voeltz 1996 reports six dialects (three per country) of unknown relationship.
